title: Disclosure benchmark: measured results
terms: benchmark results macro f1 accuracy score sentiment evaluation US India gap
text: The checked-in benchmark/metrics.json reports 128 labeled rows, split into 64 US and 64 India rows. US macro-F1 is 0.7167224080 (about 0.717) and India macro-F1 is 0.6534621578 (about 0.653); the US-minus-India gap is 0.0632602502. US accuracy is 0.84375 and India accuracy is 0.765625. These are pilot benchmark results, not a general production accuracy guarantee. Label provenance must be read with the separate provenance record.

title: Disclosure benchmark: label provenance and scope
terms: benchmark labels gold human annotation limitations dataset documents pilot
text: The README labels this a pilot/proof of concept: 32 documents and 128 benchmark chunks. Its gold-label provenance is AI-adjudicated, not independently hand-labeled. The research question is cross-market generalization across matched US/India companies; the reported gap is not an independently human-validated production accuracy figure.

title: Disclosure RAG: query retrieval and market filter
terms: question vector similarity top k filter market rag retrieve pgvector Gemini
text: retrieve_top_k embeds the question with Gemini using task_type="retrieval_query", then calls the Supabase match_chunks RPC with query_embedding and match_count. An optional market supplies filter_market. The default k is 5. This is retrieval at request time; embedding/ingesting the stored corpus is a separate preparation workflow.

title: Detector: uncertainty-gated refinement formula
terms: uncertain uncertainty confidence gate formula sigma refinement boxes 0.5 exp
text: The confidence gate is exp(-((conf - 0.5)^2)/(2 * refinement_sigma^2)); refinement_sigma defaults to 0.12. Confidence is sigmoid(objectness logits). The gate peaks near confidence 0.5 and scales learned MLP corrections to objectness, box offsets and class logits. It is not a second independent detector or proof of improved mAP.

title: Detector: decoding, confidence and NMS
terms: inference boxes decode confidence non maximum suppression nms score
text: decode_predictions converts grid box predictions into normalized xyxy boxes. The score combines sigmoid objectness with the maximum softmax class probability; confidence filtering and torchvision NMS then remove weak/overlapping candidates. The loss utilities and inference path describe mechanics, not a measured production mAP score.

title: Detector: training prerequisites and result limits
terms: training dataset missing checkpoint benchmark results score map production
text: Training imports KITTIDataset, split construction and class-frequency helpers from src.data. That package is absent in the reviewed tree even though the README lists it. A runnable training setup needs that implementation restored and inference needs a trained checkpoint. The reviewed evidence does not report a verified production mAP score; do not invent an accuracy improvement over the CNN baseline.

title: Nexus: WebSocket authentication and per-destination access
terms: websocket stomp connect subscribe send authorization private membership channel document token
text: The STOMP interceptor requires a Bearer token on CONNECT and resolves local JWT or Clerk identity. SEND and SUBSCRIBE require an authenticated user. Channel access checks organization membership, team membership when applicable, and channel membership for PRIVATE channels. Document destinations check organization/team membership and exclude soft-deleted documents. Authentication alone does not imply permission to every room.

title: Nexus: HTTP security boundaries
terms: security bcrypt password jwt token auth authentication public protected routes
text: Spring Security supplies BCryptPasswordEncoder and protects ordinary API requests with authenticated(). Explicit auth, public forms/shared files, health, docs and WebSocket handshake paths are permitted at the HTTP boundary. JWT and optional Clerk identity filters handle request identity. A public WebSocket handshake still has STOMP authentication and destination authorization; do not interpret permitAll on /ws as unrestricted room access.

title: Nexus: scoped workspace requests
terms: organization workspace team tasks docs persistence actor scope REST
text: WorkspaceController resolves the current user and organization context for workspace operations, queries organization-scoped records and writes audit events. Its endpoints work with workspace domain records through JdbcTemplate. This is evidence of implemented request scoping and persistence, not a verified statement of the author’s personal reason for choosing Java or Spring.

title: BB84 messenger: what key generation actually does
terms: quantum qkd actual simulation random hash pair keys end to end security
text: bb84_protocol hashes Python random values with SHA-256 and returns a binary string; it does not implement actual quantum key distribution. xor_encrypt_decrypt XORs UTF-8 bytes using repeated individual binary key digits and stores Base64. shared_keys is a server-memory dictionary indexed by the sorted user pair. This educational path should not be called secure end-to-end quantum messaging.

title: BB84 messenger: send payload and exposure
terms: send message plaintext key encrypted payload socket delivery security leakage
text: The send_message socket handler generates/gets a server-held key, stores an encoded message, and emits a payload containing the original plaintext message, encrypted form and key. That means the server handles plaintext and supplies the key; encrypted database text alone does not make the design end-to-end encrypted. This is distinct from the portfolio Alice/Bob/Eve demonstration.

title: SecureVault: password derivation and item encryption
terms: protect saved passwords encryption decrypt master key salt iterations pbkdf2 aes iv
text: Web Crypto derives a non-extractable 256-bit AES-GCM key with PBKDF2-SHA-256 and 100,000 iterations. generateSalt uses 16 random bytes; generateIV uses a random 12-byte IV. Vault item objects are JSON-encoded and encrypted/decrypted locally. Ciphertext and IV can be persisted, while this encryption mechanism alone is not a security audit of authentication or deployment.

title: SecureVault: reload, lock and demo bypass
terms: refresh reload persist browser localstorage master key unlock verifier rehydrate demo bypass
text: The Zustand auth store partialize persists user, salt, keyVerifier and isAuthenticated in localStorage, but does not persist masterKey. lock() clears masterKey. After refreshing, rehydrateSession derives a new candidate key and normally checks the encrypted verifier. The reviewed code also has a demo/Demo password bypass and initializes a local-vault user with isAuthenticated=true. Describe these as demo-specific behavior, not production authentication guarantees.

title: SecureVault: registration verifier
terms: register login server password salt encrypted verifier authentication
text: Registration validates the email, salt and encrypted verifier fields and their Base64 format, then calls vaultDB.register with the encryptedData and IV verifier payload. The request contract does not ask for the plaintext master password. This route describes verifier storage, not an audited production session/authentication guarantee.

title: TheMovie: offline model versus live personalization
terms: retrain online watches ratings feedback recommendations learning model SVD tf idf MovieLens
text: The shipped movie-to-movie graph combines MovieLens user-rating SVD similarity, title/genre/tag TF-IDF similarity and Bayesian rating quality. The live Next.js personalization layer combines graph neighbors with the current user feedback; the graph itself does not retrain whenever a user watches or rates a title. MovieLens has no TV interaction data. Opt-in application feedback is a separate offline export/training/promotion pipeline.

title: TheMovie: measured recommendation results
terms: NDCG recall precision hit rate normalization benchmark results improvement validation test raw
text: The corrected temporal evaluation reports test NDCG@20 0.09228, Recall@20 0.04106, Precision@20 0.085 and hit rate 0.50 for the raw SVD baseline. Only 14 validation and 30 test users qualify. Centered/scaled normalization did not beat that baseline; RATING_NORMALIZATION stays raw and shipped artifacts remain unchanged. These small returning-user-cohort results are not a general production performance claim.

title: TheMovie: request-time ranking and graph blend
terms: recommendation personalize backend Flask Next.js blend weights seed limit rank
text: The active /api/ai-recommend route is a Next.js handler that imports static recommendation, feedback and search-index artifacts. It blends the existing graph at weight 0.8 with the feedback graph at weight 1, parses bounded seed/candidate IDs and invokes rankRecommendations. It does not call a Flask inference server or train a model on each request.

title: Desktop Neo: speech recognition and voice output
terms: voice microphone speech recognizer recognition google pyttsx3 offline online internet
text: The desktop Python Neo initializes pyttsx3 for speech output. Its microphone recognizer adjusts for ambient noise and calls recognize_google(audio, language="en-US"). Therefore the recognition path uses Google speech recognition and should not be described as fully offline. This project is separate from the portfolio chatbot named Neo.

title: Desktop Neo: command routing rather than an LLM
terms: llm intelligence AI phrase commands dispatcher if elif windows controls
text: The main desktop assistant loop dispatches recognized text through explicit if/elif phrase checks for website/file opening, searches, alarms, weather, volume, shutdown and other actions. This inspected command path is a phrase dispatcher, not an LLM chat-completion backend. Several actions are Windows-specific; they run with the desktop user permissions.

title: Shikshan: teacher attendance update and scope
terms: college erp attendance marking duplicate student date teacher assigned classes SQLAlchemy
text: The teacher attendance route requires the teacher role, resolves assigned class IDs, validates the chosen date and rejects an unassigned class. For each student it queries Attendance by student_id and date, updates an existing row or inserts a new row, then commits the batch. This application-level check is not a claim of an atomic uniqueness constraint against concurrent requests.

title: Shikshan: relational records
terms: college school erp SQLAlchemy database students teachers attendance fee exams library schema
text: The Flask SQLAlchemy model layer includes User, Teacher, Student, Class, Subject, Attendance, Exam, Mark, Fee, TimeTable, Book, BookIssue and role/permission records. A student has attendance, marks and fees relationships; Attendance stores student/date/status data. The reviewed app supports PostgreSQL or local SQLite configuration rather than storing these records in Clerk metadata.

title: Attendify: metadata persistence and default accounts
terms: attendance tracker store database React Express Clerk metadata records user profile
text: DataService loads the signed-in Clerk user and reads user.privateMetadata.attendify. It returns default profile/subjects/timetable data for an empty account without writing until an explicit save. save operations update Clerk private metadata rather than a separate React database. The profile attendance requirement defaults to 75 and is normalized/clamped to 0–100.

title: Attendify: cross-device calendar exclusions
terms: holiday merge cancellation different devices calendar holidayDates cancelledDates date keyed concurrency
text: CalendarService stores exclusions in privateMetadata.attendify_calendar. It normalizes valid YYYY-MM-DD dates, deduplicates holidays/cancellations, and applies date-keyed holidayDates and cancelledDates patches so devices editing different dates avoid replacing the entire collection. isExcluded checks a holiday or a subject-specific cancellation. This is not a claim of a database-wide transaction across all attendance operations.

title: EventHub: Razorpay signature verification
terms: payment razorpay order signature hmac sha256 verification paid token
text: The Razorpay verification route computes HMAC-SHA256 over razorpay_order_id + "|" + razorpay_payment_id using the server secret, compares it with razorpay_signature and rejects a mismatch. On success it generates a QR token and marks the ticket paid, with an in-memory update fallback if the database fails. Signature checking is not a guarantee that every payment/provider integration is production-ready.

title: EventHub: check-in and duplicate race limitation
terms: qr scanner duplicates concurrent atomic transaction checkin undo lookup write
text: The check-in POST looks up a ticket by ID or token and then updates checkedIn/checkedInAt in a separate Prisma operation; action=undo reverses it. On database failure it checks the process-memory ticket store. This lookup-then-write code is not atomic duplicate-scan prevention under concurrency, and memory fallback is temporary rather than durable PostgreSQL storage.

title: EventHub: PhonePe creation is mocked
terms: phonepe provider mock payment integration status real
text: The PhonePe createPayment helper returns a mock payment URL in this source snapshot. Do not describe PhonePe creation as a verified real gateway integration. The actual Razorpay verification path is separate and must be described separately.

title: Editorial: Yjs persistence and update size
terms: collaboration crdt sync conflict merge yjs state persistence reload devices debounce 350 size
text: Yjs documents are cached per document ID and initialized from Base64 state in Supabase document_collaboration_states. Non-database updates debounce persistence by 350 ms. Persistence encodes the full Yjs state and upserts it. Incoming updates are decoded, rejected if empty or above 2,000,000 bytes, and applied with Y.applyUpdate. This supports shared CRDT state, not a claim of instantaneous durable writes.

title: Editorial: collaboration permissions and fallback
terms: viewer commenter edit permission socket join sync yjs realtime authentication access deny
text: Socket collaboration authenticates users, checks document access for sync and permits updates only to roles other than viewer/commenter. yjs-sync-request returns the persisted/shared state through getCollaborationState; yjs-update applies and broadcasts updates to the room. If Yjs sync is unavailable, yjs-unavailable allows an older full-document transport. The source does not promise offline synchronization for every failure.

title: Editorial: rename without losing local edits
terms: document rename title local unsaved edit active doc store upsert
text: renameDocument trims and rejects an empty title, PUTs the new title to /docs/{id}, then merges the returned title/updatedAt into the current active/local document before upserting it. This avoids replacing a newer locally edited document body with an older rename response.

title: UNIX scheduler: waiting/turnaround metrics
terms: cpu scheduler algorithms FCFS SJF Priority Round Robin RR waiting turnaround completion formula
text: The C scheduler calculates turnaround = completion - arrival, and waiting = turnaround - burst. It implements FCFS, SJF, Priority and Round Robin (RR), with arrival-aware scheduling and Gantt/metric output for the Zenity UI. These are educational scheduling simulations, not changes to the host kernel scheduler.

title: UNIX toolkit: network throughput sampling
terms: linux utility suite interface network throughput RX TX bytes counters monitor
text: The Bash network monitor finds a default network interface, reads RX/TX byte counters from sysfs, and reports interval receive/transmit throughput. It samples rx_bytes and tx_bytes for the selected interface, rather than packet inspection or a remote analytics backend. It requires the host Linux tools and a desktop/terminal environment.

title: UNIX toolkit: process termination checks
terms: process manager kill terminate PID confirmation SIGTERM ps validation
text: The C process manager lists processes, validates the chosen PID, requests a Zenity confirmation and then sends SIGTERM with kill(). It does not use a default SIGKILL and does not terminate a process merely because the visitor opens the portfolio demo. Actual permissions and process state determine whether the local operation succeeds.
